verdicts.note: All-girls school and 'us girls' framing throughout confirm female.
'All girls Grammar' directly = single sex.
'industrial design & technology' = Design & Technology.
'a lot more exciting' / interesting work; agree well supported.
Repeated 'so broad and varied... what I was looking for' supports strongly agree.
Quote is engineering-vs-graphics, not science/maths specifically; 'without specialising' spirit present but thin.
Mum interior design/textiles, dad fashion = family in the industry.
Gave interest but did not encourage the choice; disagree fits 'mother encouraged me'.
Careers advice 'not that helpful'; not encouraging = disagree.
Quote is about DT being a best subject at GCSE, not being good at maths AND science; variable not supported by this quote.
School refused to run DT A level (steered to maths/science); she petitioned — counts as discouragement/obstruction = yes.
'They' = the school/institution; ambiguous vs teachers but 'other' defensible. Confidence already low.
Switched to sandwich course, applying; intends to go = yes.
Names experience as 'the best thing'; strongly agree fits.
'a taster for what I want to do' = idea of what industry is like.
Framed as 'another good thing' / out of debt; borderline 3 vs 4, 'out of debt' tilts to agree but weak.
'always need min 1 year experience... easy way to get that' = improve job chances.
'hoping... will help me decide' directly supports.
'get better marks in the final year' = improve grades on return.
'not just work wise but also personally' = personal development.
'need to have a great idea for a final project' linked to placement = help decide final-year project.
Peers doing it / longer student life are non-compulsory extra reasons = other.
'yes - still... I do really enjoy it' = pleased (agree, caveat on workload).
Quote about girls being neater does not support 'students are competitive'; she only calls the field/job market competitive, not students. No verbatim support for this variable.
'guys tend to be a lot more confident than the girls... and it shows' = strongly agree.
'male lecturers are more helpful to the girls' = female students get more help.
Group work 'taught me for the future' re team problems = develops interpersonal skills.
'lot of deadlines in, at the same time' = competing deadlines, strongly agree.
'more bonded... I really like that', named best thing = very satisfied.
'so broad and varied... what I was looking for' = very satisfied with variety.
'more teaching hours so gaining a lot more' frames it positively = satisfied.
Amount of coursework named 'the worst thing'; dissatisfied despite mild 'I like always having work' caveat.
Tutor approachable but rarely seen, would be put off with personal issues = neutral.
'needs to be done, just not always great' = mixed/neutral.
'working in a consultancy appeals to me the most' = consultancy.
Rejects management, prefers being part of the group = technical/specialist (non-managerial).
'appealing when they have extra training' = training important.
'better to work as a team' = people worked with important.
'live in London... like to move back there and work' = clear location preference, important.
'comfortable money wise' + 'not particularly ambitious' = money matters only modestly; important is thin. Confidence already low.
